newsitem.title: UK: Most 1997-8 spending issues settled - UK Treasury.
newsitem.headline: Most 1997-8 spending issues settled - UK Treasury.

text.p: The British Treasury on Tuesday would not comment on domestic press reports that it had come to a compromise with the Department of Health on future spending for the National Health Service.
But a spokesman said that agreement had been reached with most government departments on spending totals for 1997-8 ahead of a cabinet meeting to discuss the issue which is due to start at 1000 gmt.
"The overwhelming majority of people have settled and it will go to cabinet today," the spokesman said.
He said it could take more than one cabinet meeting to reach a final agreement, but that would be quite normal.

Some Conservative MPs are convinced the political fortunes of the government hang on how much the so-called control total for total government spending can be squeezed below the 268.2 billion pound ($439.2 billion) target in last year's budget.

Some British newspapers on Tuesday reported that Health Secretary Stephen Dorrell had won about half the one billion stg in extra health service spending he had been seeking in meetings with Chief Secretary to the Treasury William Waldegrave.
The government has to agree on spending for all departments in time for Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke to frame his November 26 budget statement.
The more spending can be restrained, the greater is likely to be Clarke's elbow room for voter-pleasing tax cuts ahead of a general election which must be held by May 22.
But even if agreement were reached on Tuesday, the government would not announce its spending plans until Clarke makes his budget statement.
They are traditionally published in the Red Book which accompanies the budget, the Treasury spokesman noted. ($1=.6107 Pound)
